entries.method: Exact S4 fixed-point integer DP on 15 nonzero mask orbit classes, 15 partition Möbius inverse, Burnside quotient
entries.null_model: Uniform legal-ticket combinatorial universe (mathematical structure only; no draw-time null inference)
entries.primary_endpoint: Independent 2,957 valid unlabeled membership structures, from 52,450 labeled nonnegative and 50,985 labeled distinct-bet solutions
entries.result_summary: Independent identity fixed 50,985, full 24-permutation fixed-point numerator 70,968 and 70,968/24=2,957; validates original structural count, not independently official-prize optimum nor forecast.
entries.research_question: Can a mathematically independent S4 Burnside and Mobius integer-DP certificate verify that the original exact four-ticket overlap structure classifier has exactly 2957 distinct unlabeled classes?
entries.hypothesis: Fixed points of S4 on legal 15-mask degree-six vectors, corrected for equal ticket rows via partition-lattice Mobius, must give exactly the same 2957 structural orbits as the original enumerator.
limitations: Confirms only the structural-class count; not an independent re-implementation of official eight-tier prize scoring for each class or of global optimality.
Structural exactness cannot imply a future lottery prediction advantage, a larger jackpot chance for a fixed ticket, or a change to any already bought selection.
Full v0.25 multivariate covariance, Pareto and future-only objectives in Issue #8 remain open.
entries.next_action: Reuse this independent count to strengthen four-ticket class enumeration audits; continue genuinely distinct unfinished #8 objectives without modifying source data or pre-draw seals.

entries.research_question: Can all 163 exact-fair 6/49 feature covariance entries, including 49 number memberships, Sum/OddCount/Span, L1/L2/L3 taxonomy, be calculated as exact rational numbers without Monte Carlo approximation?
entries.hypothesis: Exhaustive independent L3 scalar graph census and exact analytic number/extrema identities will agree with the pinned v0.16 full-universe shape fixture, yielding 13,366 exact upper-triangle second moments over all C(49,6) tickets.
entries.source_cutoff: Fair mathematical universe of all 13,983,816 6-of-49 combinations (not a historical draw cutoff)
entries.model_version: v0.25 P0 full 163-feature exact population covariance — scalar C++ census + Python integer reconstruction
entries.null_model: Exact IID uniform 6/49 finite-population combinatorial reference, sampling without replacement within each six-number ticket
entries.multiple_testing: NOT_APPLICABLE — exact theoretical integer moment enumeration, no empirical hypothesis test
entries.primary_endpoint: All 13,366 integer upper-triangle raw moments and exact rational covariance for 163 features, validated against original complete 6/11/94 taxonomy
entries.result_summary: All 13,983,816 legal combinations enumerated. 163 features and 13,366 upper-triangle exact raw moments. Exact original v0.16 94 L3 plus 11 L2 and 6 L1 class counts match; number marginal C(48,5), span mean 250/7 and Sum variance 1075 independently verified. CI eight tests PASS. This confirms a theoretical reference only, not forecast skill.
entries.method: Standalone C++17 six-vertex BFS full universe with 94 sufficient-statistic rows, independent Python hypergeometric/extrema moments, exact L3→L2→L1 nesting and original SHA-pinned v0.16 class fixture; no history outcomes.
limitations: The exact 163x163 matrix is singular from number size, Sum/OddCount linear dependence and nested Shape one-hots. Downstream covariance inverse requires a declared and validated regularization or dimensional reduction.
The existing v0.25 MC-estimated covariance and its historical optimizer/selections are not silently changed or reevaluated by this reference-only work.
Exact fair-IID covariance is a mathematical null, not evidence that the lottery is physically fair, that historical deficits must compensate, or that any candidate ticket becomes more likely to win.
All full-dimensional Monte Carlo-versus-exact optimizer comparisons, Pareto tradeoffs and prospective evidence within #8 remain separately pending.
entries.next_action: Run a matched fixed-budget comparison of existing MC covariance and new exact theory with stable ridge/rank handling and whole-pipeline IID null. Do not use already observed historical outcomes as new prospective confirmation.

entries.research_question: Does replacing sample covariance with exact fair-IID covariance produce an unusually large gain in the same four-ticket descriptive repair search?
entries.hypothesis: The exact-covariance-selected portfolio has a lower common exact post-augmentation distance than the matched-MC-selected portfolio, by more than typically found when both selectors run on fair-IID histories.
entries.model_version: v0.25 fixed-budget exact versus MC covariance benchmark v1
entries.null_model: 99 independent histories of 2,497 IID uniform 6/49 draws, paired across all three covariance arms
entries.multiple_testing: One predeclared primary contrast within the retrospective benchmark; the legacy contrast and within-arm gains are diagnostic
entries.primary_endpoint: Common exact post-augmentation distance of matched MC portfolio minus distance of Exact portfolio
entries.result_summary: All three models selected the same four tickets. Primary gain 0.0, 89/99 paired IID gains at least as large, add-one upper-tail p=0.90. The legacy result reproduced the prior observed and null mean gains.
entries.method: Common 163-feature registry, exact means, fixed 300-ticket pool, selector seed 649, ridge 0.25 and bounded legacy search. Shared exact scaling isolates covariance; legacy scaling is included for reproduction.
limitations: Retrospective descriptive objective under one cutoff, one candidate pool and one fixed 8,192-ticket covariance sample.
Bounded search does not certify global optimality, and the 99 conditional IID replicates limit tail resolution.
The experiment has no future outcomes or predictive endpoint.
entries.next_action: Use versioned independent cutoffs or a predeclared no-lookahead walk-forward when testing selection robustness, and keep future-only forecast evaluation tied to an independent endpoint.

entries.research_question: Does Exact covariance improve holdout award incidence compared with Matched MC at identical fair-IID official prize coverage?
entries.hypothesis: Exact wins on more held-out draws than Matched MC by an amount unusually large under whole-pipeline IID replay.
entries.null_model: 99 IID six-main-plus-special histories, with all three optimizers rerun in each of the eight folds
entries.multiple_testing: One primary Exact minus Matched MC upper-tail contrast; other arms and absolute effect are diagnostic
entries.primary_endpoint: Number of holdout draws with any eight-tier award for Exact minus Matched MC
entries.result_summary: Exact 22/200, Matched MC and Legacy MC 25/200 each, history-blind baseline 22/200. Observed primary delta -3 draws, empirical upper-tail p=0.91. Exact and Matched MC selected identical portfolios in seven of eight folds.
entries.method: Expanding chronological prefixes, eight disjoint 25-draw holdouts, common legacy candidate pool and search, exact disjoint coverage parity, shared exact scaling in the primary contrast, verified bonus scoring.
limitations: The original historical fold scheme and outcomes have been used for prior research.
One bounded optimizer, one fixed sample covariance, one timeline, 200 tested draws and 99 paired null replays limit inference.
All four arms have identical theoretical fair-IID award incidence. Prospective prediction requires separately frozen evidence.
entries.next_action: Use a separately specified unseen prospective evaluation if a future covariance strategy has a prespecified discriminating endpoint.

entries.primary_endpoint: N times ridge-whitened squared distance from the exact fair feature mean

entries.method: Exact population covariance and fair categorical masses, standardized ridge 0.25, chronological segment-matched IID replay, and bias estimates for plug-in entropy.

The size check conditions on one finite null reference, and the adjusted test targets the declared feature family only.
entries.next_action: Use a prospective design only after the eligibility, exact cross-arm discordance and power checks have been recorded.

entries.research_question: How do exact fair main-ball threshold coverage and historical covariance-aware repair trade off in a fixed four-ticket search?
entries.hypothesis: Some portfolios improve historical repair at lower coverage, while exact coverage maxima can be certified independently by overlap structure.
entries.model_version: v0.25 joint coverage and exact covariance Pareto v1
entries.null_model: Uniform six-of-49 finite universe; separate exact special-ball prize calculation
entries.multiple_testing: Objective enumeration and descriptive ranking; no statistical hypothesis test
entries.primary_endpoint: Nondominated vectors across bounded historical repair searches, and exact 3+/4+/5+ coverage maxima across all 2,957 structural orbits
entries.result_summary: Six matched-pool strategies, 6,781 evaluated complete portfolios and 22 frontier vectors. The disjoint orbit uniquely maximizes the three main-ball coverage thresholds jointly. Independent full enumeration matched the joint DP on two generated portfolios.
entries.method: 300-ticket seeded pool, fixed budget, deterministic one-ticket swaps, exact population covariance with ridge 0.25, and membership-mask counts checked against full-universe enumeration.
limitations: The repair frontier covers evaluated portfolios only and uses one historical cutoff.
Exact structural maxima describe the fair mathematical model. No outcome prediction was evaluated.
entries.next_action: Complete remaining finite-sample descriptive calibration and retain independent prospective protocol requirements.
